NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a mechanical cleaning procedure to remove biofilm and scale.
CALCULATED: Proposed mechanism departs by using electrochemical modulation to prevent adhesion rather than physical removal.
PHYSICS CHECK: Electrostatic repulsion between charged surfaces and biofilm precursors prevents initial adhesion, governed by DLVO theory. Verification: Zeta potential measurements showing >30mV repulsion between plates and biofilm precursors under flow conditions.

PHYSICS CHECK
GOVERNING RELATION: DLVO theory for colloidal stability - energy barrier = (64×c×R×T²×γ²×κ⁻¹)/(1000×ε×ε₀)
CALCULATED: For stainless steel in cooling water with γ=0.05C/m², κ=10⁷ m⁻¹, energy barrier >15kT prevents adhesion
ASSUMPTION: Cooling water conductivity is within typical range (500-1500 μS/cm)

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Titanium electrode mesh (same class as existing sacrificial anodes) - installed on inlet side of each plate
2. DC power supply (same class as existing cathodic protection systems) - 5V output, 1A max per plate
3. Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) insulating gaskets (same class as existing gaskets)
4. Control system (same class as existing building automation) - potential monitoring, automatic polarity reversal every 48 hours
ASSUMPTION: Existing electrical infrastructure can support additional low-voltage DC loads

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- INSTALLABILITY: Comparable to existing cathodic protection installation (same class)
- OPERABILITY: No additional operator training required (same class as existing automated systems)
- MAINTENANCE: Electrode inspection during regular maintenance (same class as existing anode replacement)
- COST CLASS: Capital cost similar to existing protection systems (same class), operational cost <10% increase for electricity
- ADVANTAGE: Eliminates need for mechanical cleaning shutdowns

EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL: Install test unit in parallel with operational heat exchanger with identical flow conditions. Apply electrochemical modulation at 5V with 48-hour polarity reversal. Monitor heat transfer coefficient and pressure drop weekly.
INSTRUMENTS: Temperature sensors (in/out), flow meter, pressure transducers, heat transfer calculation software
PASS/AILURE THRESHOLD: Heat transfer coefficient must remain >2500 W/m2K for 12 months without exceeding 0.5 ppm residual chlorine
DURATION: 12 months continuous operation
KILL CRITERION: If heat transfer coefficient drops below 2500 W/m2K at any point, test fails
